comparison_scope: One known saved bug case, one response per model per output cap. Not blinded human annotation or a model-quality benchmark.

mini.finding: Uses a past expected fix plan, but gives no dates and does not explicitly preserve unknown released-fix status before suggesting a fresh report on 3.2 or later.

gpt_5_6.finding: Dates September and December 2025 expectations, distinguishes the later closure, attributes the historical pin and preserves release uncertainty. The proposed final-release verification could still explicitly say if available.

mini.finding: Describes early teardown, but omits the reporter's clarification that real callbacks were already idempotent, while repeating the multiple-invocation warning.

gpt_5_6.finding: Explicitly records idempotence and the illustrative use of g.pop, and does not ask for those facts again or renew the redundant callback advice in the draft.

mini.finding: Uses only the read candidate and correct source pair, with supported differences, but says both are regressions without a retrieved before/after version comparison for #6123.

gpt_5_6.finding: Uses the same read candidate and source pair, distinguishes the reported failure conditions, and avoids calling the candidate a verified regression.

mini.finding: Only bug is recommended with target/catalog citations and consistent prose.

gpt_5_6.finding: Only bug is recommended with target/catalog citations and consistent prose. Label relevance remains a judgment, not a documented policy guarantee.

mini.finding: No first-person reproduction, repository mutation or explicit closure-to-fix claim appears.

gpt_5_6.finding: No invented action or execution, and explicit separation of closure from a shipped fix.

additional_source_coverage_observation.mini: known_facts[3] says the thread was fully read on page 1, without acknowledging the supplied S5 clipping notice. This overstates text coverage; eight retrieved comments is not all original text.
additional_source_coverage_observation.gpt_5_6: Distinguishes all eight comments retrieved from one clipped comment and limits statements about the 3.2.0.dev0 test to visible content.
additional_source_coverage_observation.automated_check_disagreement: Both raw known_comment_claims_supported values are true. Preserve them; the assistant separately flags the mini coverage wording.

quality_conclusion: GPT-5.6 is more cautious and better uses dates, the reporter clarification and evidence limits in this case. Mini is concise and gets the core issue, candidate differences and bug label right, but leaves important source-use gaps.
budget_conclusion: Both complete at 4800 in this run. Mini uses 2474 output tokens, above 2400; GPT-5.6 uses 2083, below 2400. These are different sampled responses from the prior round, not fixed token requirements or universal sufficiency.
cost_and_latency_note: Mini: 18.31s and USD 0.01195875 basic standard estimate; GPT-5.6: 23.35s and USD 0.0453368. Both had large cache hits (8960/9162) and zero cache-write tokens. Do not attribute lower cost than the first round solely to model efficiency or infer average latency from one sample.
decision: Continue using the user-selected GPT-5.6/medium as the quality-first trial baseline, without changing production's 2400 cap or claiming M2 acceptance.
next_recommended_step: Check the two other saved issue types with GPT-5.6/medium and the unchanged 2400 application output cap before returning to full M2 live-loop acceptance.
